Synopsis:
Sinopec is aggressively extending its Russian oil purchases (primarily ESPO blend, plus Sokol and Urals) into October and beyond, locking in discounted barrels to maximize refining margins and fuel export volumes. This has crowded out China's independent teapot refiners, who simultaneously face sharply reduced Iranian supply due to a U.S. naval blockade reinstated in mid-July 2026. ESPO premiums are surging, Iranian Light is trading at historically atypical premiums, and alternative grades (Iraqi Basrah Medium, Brazilian, Canadian) are also spiking. Teapots face margin compression and may be forced to cut refinery runs as inventories are estimated to last only until late September/early October.

Q05. Is the content describing effects very directly impacting Europe and/or European energy markets?
Relevance: The article does note Urals loadings from Russian European ports as part of Sinopec's buying programme. If Sinopec is absorbing Urals volumes that might otherwise flow into European-adjacent markets, this could tighten crude availability marginally, but the article frames this as a minor component of Sinopec's broader Russian crude strategy. No direct European energy market impact is discussed. The connection to German Power or European gas is negligible.
